snippet.title: AI Lead Generation That Runs Every Morning (Free Open-Source Scraper) #Shorts
snippet.description:
AI lead generation with GPT-6 Astra and ScrapeGraphAI, a free, open-source AI web scraper: new UK company leads land in one sheet every morning at 7.
Free guide: https://withhammad.com/resources/scrapegraphai-lead-finder (setup, code, prompts and the UK rules)

How this B2B lead generation setup works:
1. ScrapeGraphAI (MIT licence, 31k+ GitHub stars) reads each company website and returns only the fields you ask for, as clean rows. It runs on a free local model through Ollama, so you don't pay per lead.
2. Give GPT-6 Astra (or Claude Code) the repo and say who to find, e.g. 200 UK online shops that are registered companies.
3. Save the process as a skill and a ChatGPT scheduled task at 07:00, and new leads are added to the same sheet each morning.

What's free and what isn't: the scraper and the local model are free; GPT-6 Astra needs a paid ChatGPT plan (Claude Code also needs a paid Claude plan or API credits). A free macOS launchd job can run the script every morning instead. A local run needs your computer awake, and the ChatGPT desktop app open for a scheduled task.

Business contacts only (limited companies; sole traders need consent). Respect robots.txt and site terms, put your name and an opt-out in every email, and check the rows before you send anything. Not legal advice.

Repo: https://github.com/ScrapeGraphAI/Scrapegraph-ai

Commented HARVEST? There are no DMs on YouTube, so here's the guide: https://withhammad.com/resources/scrapegraphai-lead-finder

snippet.title: How to Choose an LLM for AI Agents: Evaluation, Cost & Reliability
snippet.description:
Learn how to choose an LLM for AI agents using evaluation cases, cost per successful task, latency and reliability checks. This 20-minute AI engineering guide follows a fictional equipment service assistant from workflow design to a release decision.

For software developers and AI engineers working with OpenAI, Anthropic, tool calling and retrieval. The focus is on designing a useful comparison, checking failures and deciding what evidence your application needs.

You’ll learn how to:
• Write acceptance criteria and evaluation cases.
• Check tool permissions, structured outputs and retrieved sources.
• Compare cost, latency and retry behavior.
• Plan human approval, tracing and rollback.

The scenario and records are synthetic. No model benchmark, winning model or deployed client result is claimed. Model-release context reflects research on 3 October 2026.

snippet.title: I Built an Autonomous AI Agent for Google Ads (Live, Real Client, Full Walkthrough)
snippet.description:
I built Ads OS — an AI system that manages a real Google Ads account autonomously. It's live today, running against a real client's ad spend.

Most "AI ads agents" ask you to trust a black box. This one doesn't get that trust by default: every proposed change passes a guardrails layer before it can touch the account, every mutation writes a rollback record before it executes, and nothing runs live until it's proven itself in shadow mode first.

In this video: a full walkthrough of the actual product — real voice interface, real account data pulled from the Google Ads API, live decision queue, full audit trail, and the safety architecture that makes autonomous ad management something you can actually trust.

Built solo, deployed end-to-end, currently managing a real client account.

If you're building AI agents, doing performance marketing, or just curious what "autonomous but safe" actually looks like in practice — this is that, not a mockup.
